newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk traders see 200,000T cotton imports in spring.
newsitem.headline: Turk traders see 200,000T cotton imports in spring.

text.p: Turkish cotton traders said on Thursday yarn producers were likely to import 200,000 tonnes of good quality cotton in the spring because of problems with the local crop.
The government announces fixed cotton prices at the start of the harvest but does not give increments to compensate for inflation and world price changes.
"Farmers are disappointed with prices. They cannot wait until the next crop year to plant cotton. They will opt for alternative products," he said.
"We have information that some regions in the Aegean have totally given up farming cotton next year," he said.
He said Turkey's cotton production was estimated to shoot up to a record high of one million tonnes in 1996/97 from 837,000 tonnes a year ago.
Annual consumption in Turkey is about 900,000 tonnes, which leaves room for some exports.

Cotton is a key product for the self-sufficiency of Turkey's textile industry, whose exports of about $8.5 billion in 1995 were the country's top money spinner, but textile producers frequently resort to cotton imports to meet quality standards.
Hulusi Tanman, head of Aegean Farmers Association, said the producers were being forced by the government's to sell their crop at prices lower than the production cost.
"We will have to grow other products like wheat which is more profitable," he said. --Istanbul Newsroom, 90-212-275 0875
